_comment: Round 3 of the de-ossification port: the whole of Matrix33 (seventeen functions) and the whole
of Matrix66 (eleven), in code/midtown2/vector7/matrix33.cpp and matrix66.cpp. Both classes are
complete - the map has exactly twenty-eight symbols across the two, all of them functions,
there is no static and no vftable in either, and none is left as ARTS_IMPORT.
tools/build.py folds every data/ported_*.json into data/ported.json at step 1, before it runs
genheaders.py and before tools/asm.py, so this file only has to sit in data/ - do not merge it
by hand. The headers are already flipped to ARTS_EXPORT, and asm.py stops the build on an
export that ported.json does not list, so the two must travel together.
LAYOUTS. Neither class has an entry in MM2_RE_KIT's _ALL_TYPES.h, so neither was in
data/layouts.json. They are now, added from data/layouts_vector7_round3.json, which carries
the full derivation. That file is not optional bookkeeping: build.py re-runs genheaders.py on
every build, and genheaders emits members and check_size from layouts.json alone - with no
entry there it would strip the members out of both headers and matrix33.cpp would stop
compiling. Both headers as committed are byte-identical to what genheaders now regenerates,
so a build is a no-op on them.
Matrix33 = 0x24, nine f32 in row-major order. ?Set@Matrix33@@QAEXABV1@@Z (0x496230) copies
exactly nine dwords, +0x00 through +0x20, and stops; ?Inverse@Matrix33@@QAEXABV1@@Z
(0x4969D0) makes room for one with `sub esp, 0x24`; ?Inverse@Matrix33@@QAEXXZ (0x4968B0)
copies its result home with `mov ecx, 9; rep movsd`; and an earlier automated pass reached
the same 0x24 independently - data/layouts_from_serialization.json has Matrix33 with a
size_lower_bound of 36 from that same memcpy, graded WEAK and never merged. The mNN naming
is fixed by ?CrossProduct@Matrix33@@QAEXABVVector3@@@Z (0x496750), which is the skew matrix
of `arg1 % v` under this reading and its negation under the transposed one.
Matrix66 = 0x90, four Matrix33 blocks at 0x00/0x24/0x48/0x6C. Every method in the class is a
sequence of Matrix33 calls at those four offsets and nothing else; ?Inverse@Matrix66@@QAEXXZ
allocates a whole one with `sub esp, 0x90`. Which block is which is fixed by
?Dot@Matrix66@@QAEXABV1@@Z, whose new 0x00 block is (0x00 * a.0x00) + (0x24 * a.0x48) - the
2x2 block product only if 0x24 is the (0,1) block and 0x48 the (1,0) block - and confirmed
independently by ?Transpose@Matrix66@@QAEXABV1@@Z, which swaps 0x24 with 0x48 and leaves
0x00 and 0x6C on the diagonal.
EVIDENCE. Every body was disassembled with capstone 5.0.7 over the bytes of midtown2.exe at
the RVA midtown2.map gives, not transcribed from MM2_RE_KIT - the kit has no type for either
class, so its pseudocode is raw `*(float *)(a1 + 20)` arithmetic and the offsets have to be
read regardless. All twenty-eight were then re-verified instruction by instruction against the
same disassembly in a second pass, including the whole of ?Inverse@Matrix66@@QAEXABV1@@Z,
whose six stack locals and two IsZero branches were traced slot by slot.
Matrix33::Dot, Matrix33::DotCrossProdMtx and the body of Matrix33::Inverse are
instruction-for-instruction Matrix34::Dot3x3, Matrix34::Dot3x3CrossProdMtx and the 3x3 half of
Matrix34::Inverse, which are already ported in matrix34.cpp from a different source; those
three were cross-checked against it and agree, including the shared warning literal at
0x5C76F8 that still reads "Matrix34::Inverse()".
TWO CORRECTIONS to the bodies, both about an unordered compare, both verified against the
instruction stream:
Matrix33::IsZero tests `test ah, 0x40` - C3 alone - after each fcomp, and C3 is set by an
equal compare AND by an unordered one, so the original treats a NaN element as a zero and
keeps scanning. `m00 != 0.0f` is true on a NaN and returned false. Now spelled as a pair of
strict compares per element. Matrix66::Inverse selects its branch on this bool, so the
divergence was reachable.
Matrix33::Inverse tests the determinant the same way, and the warn path is the C3 path, so a
NaN determinant warns and leaves the matrix alone rather than inverting. NOTE: the identical
instruction in Matrix34::Inverse (matrix34.cpp) is still the plain `v2 == 0.0` and still
diverges there; vector4.cpp's Vector4::Plane comments the same intent but `!(sq != 0.0)`
does not achieve it either. Both are pre-existing and were left alone by this round.
VERIFIERS, re-run after the corrections. py tools/verify_extents.py with these twenty-eight
merged in: 215 ported functions checked, PASS - no dword in .rdata or .data points strictly
inside any of the twenty-eight extents, which matters because Matrix33 and Matrix66 occupy one
unbroken run from 0x496230 to 0x496ECF. Every extent was also eyeballed in the disassembly and
each ends in `ret` followed only by nop padding, so no unnamed neighbour is being swallowed
(Trap 7). py tools/verify_arity.py reports no mismatch and no skip for any symbol in either
class; all twenty-eight `ret imm16` values were additionally read off the disassembly by hand
and agree with the mangled names, and each reference argument was checked for being used as an
address rather than a value, which is the Trap 14 failure the arity check cannot see.
NOT PORTED. ?Print@Quaternion@@QBEXPBD@Z (0x4C4C20) was rejected by verify_extents - data
words point at 0x4C4C44 and 0x4C4C55, inside its 64-byte extent - so the rest of Quaternion
was left alone rather than ported piecemeal.
